moc: the unfinished Monument column (fluted, inside timber scaffolding)

ghi_chu.mo_ta: The Monument column inside the timber scaffolding is a plain, smooth, pale cylinder. It shows no fluting and no recognisable Monument form such as a base or pedestal.
ghi_chu.ly_do: The unfinished Monument of 1675 should be a fluted Doric column. What is shown is not that form.

ghi_chu.mo_ta: Very large, uniform 5–6 storey red-brick blocks with regular grids of white-framed multi-pane sash windows. They look like Georgian or industrial mill buildings.
ghi_chu.ly_do: London houses in 1675 were mostly 3–4 storeys. Sash windows were only just appearing then. Flat, repetitive tall brick blocks of this kind belong to the 18th and 19th centuries.

ghi_chu.mo_ta: The right-hand blocks are tall, regular, many-windowed brick buildings with sash windows.
ghi_chu.ly_do: These are too tall and too uniform for post-Fire London in 1675. Their style is later Georgian.
